... THIRD INNINGS ...

A game on the knife-edge - With the first-innings battle concluded, the match sits on a knife-edge as the sun begins to set on Day 3. Pakistan will feel they have the momentum to make late inroads with the ball as Bangladesh faces a tricky few overs before Stumps. A 27-run lead is a slender advantage for the hosts, but on a pitch that is starting to offer more for the bowlers, every run will be worth its weight in gold. Both sides head into the final stretch of the day knowing that a couple of early wickets or a steady opening stand could dictate the course of this enthralling encounter.

The Bangladeshi Fightback - However, the momentum shifted spectacularly as the Bangladesh bowling attack found their rhythm and sparked a middle-order collapse. Led by the relentless Taskin Ahmed and the guile of Mehidy Hasan Miraz, the visitors clawed their way back into the contest. Miraz was the undisputed star of the show, weaving a web around the Pakistani batters to claim a prestigious five-wicket haul. Taskin and Taijul Islam provided excellent support with two wickets apiece, while Nahid Rana chipped in with a crucial breakthrough. This collective bowling brilliance ensured that Pakistan was eventually bowled out for 386, falling just 27 runs short of the Bangladesh total.

The debutants’ foundation - Pakistan’s pursuit of Bangladesh’s first-innings total of 413 began with immense promise. Resuming Day 3 in a commanding position at 179 for 1, the hosts looked set to eclipse the target with ease. The story of the innings was written by the debutants, Azan Awais and Abdullah Fazal, who both showed remarkable composure on the big stage. Azan celebrated his maiden outing with a magnificent century, while Fazal provided stalwart support with a gritty half-century. With Mohammad Rizwan and Agha Salman also chipping in with vital fifties of their own, Pakistan seemed destined for a massive lead.

Weather Interrupts the Momentum - The session concluded on a somber note as the dark clouds that had been hovering over the stadium finally forced the umpires to take the player off for early Tea. With rain beginning to fall and the ground staff rushing out to bring on the covers, the players were ushered off the field earlier than scheduled. The damp conditions suggest we may be in for a slightly longer delay than a standard interval, leaving the match delicately poised. Bangladesh will feel they are back in the hunt after that late breakthrough, while Pakistan will be hoping the weather clears quickly so Agha can continue his rescue act.

The new ball challenge and a late twist - As the innings progressed and Bangladesh opted for the second new ball. The atmospheric conditions made the moving delivery a tricky proposition, testing the resolve of the set batters once again. Rizwan and Agha navigated this difficult phase with maturity, surviving the initial burst of swing and seam. However, just as the session seemed to be ending in Pakistan’s favor, a lapse in judgment shifted the scales. With Tea approaching and a freshening breeze picking up, Rizwan attempted to accelerate against Taijul Islam but miscued his effort, falling just before the break and ending a vital stand.

A resilient post-Lunch recovery - The afternoon session saw a complete shift in momentum as Pakistan’s middle order finally found its footing. Mohammad Rizwan and Salman emerged from the Lunch break with clear intent, effectively neutralizing the Bangladeshi bowling threat that had caused such chaos earlier in the day. The pair batted with a perfect blend of caution and aggression, rotating the strike and finding the boundaries at a brisk clip. Their century partnership turned a potential disaster into a position of respectability, as both batters showcased excellent temperament to reach their respective half-centuries and put the pressure back on the visitors.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session. Salman Agha and Mohammad Rizwan have walked out in the middle to resume the Pakistan innings. For Bangladesh, Mehidy Hasan Miraz will open the bowling in this session.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

A critical afternoon awaits - As the players head in for the Lunch interval, the psychological edge has swung firmly toward the visitors. Bangladesh’s ability to dismantle a settled batting lineup in the blink of an eye has injected fresh life into the match, leaving the Pakistani camp searching for answers to stem the tide. The post-Lunch session will be the defining period of the day. Pakistan must rebuild through Salman’s fortunate second life, while Bangladesh will be smelling blood, eager to wrap up the tail. We will be back at 6.40 am GMT to see if Pakistan can recover or if the Tigers will continue their march.

Bangladesh’s bowling dominance - The first session undeniably belonged to Bangladesh, who transformed the contest with a ruthless display of wicket-taking. From a position of absolute comfort, Pakistan were sent reeling to 230 for 5 in a frantic period where four wickets fell for just twenty runs. Taskin Ahmed was the primary architect of this destruction, finding extra rhythm and bounce to claim two vital scalps, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz exploited the shifting momentum to pick up a brace of his own. Things could have reached a point of no return for the hosts had Salman Agha not received a massive reprieve, surviving a dismissal only because the bowler had overstepped for a No Ball.

From milestone magic to sudden chaos - The morning began with a sense of triumph for the hosts as the overnight pair of Azan and Fazal continued their clinical accumulation of runs. Resuming at 179 for 1, the spotlight stayed firmly on Azan, who etched his name into the record books by reaching a magnificent century on his Test debut. With Fazal crossing his own half-century milestone at the other end, the foundation looked unshakable at 210 for 1. However, the atmosphere shifted instantly when Azan finally fell and his departure triggered a staggering collapse that saw the middle-order crumble under a sudden barrage of disciplined bowling.

PITCH REPORT ON DAY 3 - Athar Ali Khan says that surface remains excellent for batting on this pivotal moving day, though it presents specific challenges for both sides.  Khan reckons that with seven left-handers in the Pakistan lineup, bowlers must maintain a disciplined line tight to the stumps, as the pitch offers little margin for wide deliveries. Athar mentions that while the track is currently holding up, cracks are expected to open further as play progresses, demanding that batters focus on playing strictly to the merit of the ball. Khan concludes by saying that the primary objective for the bowling attack is to remain patient and consistently keep the stumps in play to exploit any developing unevenness.

Shaheen Afridi is up for a chat - Shaheen says that the surface on the first day was a bit double-paced but on Day 2, the surface had become better for batting and their bowling unit was looking at the right areas and it worked in their favor. Shaheed credits Azan Awais and Abdullah Fazal for their solid batting display, saying they are the future and it is good to see them play well against a quality bowling unit. Shaheen adds that the first session of Day 3 will be key and if they can win it, they'll be ahead in the contest.

The path to an upper hand - To gain the upper hand today, both teams must execute their plans with surgical precision. Bangladesh's bowlers, particularly their spinners like Mehidy Hasan Miraz, need to exploit the pitch's wear to dry up runs and force mistakes. Disciplined line and length from the seamers will also be crucial to prevent the Pakistani batters from scoring freely. On the other hand, Pakistan must maintain their current composure. The set batters, Awais and Fazal, need to dig deep and bat for long periods, as every run added without losing a wicket exponentially increases the pressure on the hosts. The side that wins the morning session will likely find themselves in the driver's seat as this tactical battle unfolds.

Moving day - As we step into Day 3, the classic moving day of Test cricket, the match stands beautifully poised. Historically, this is the day where the game's direction is often decided. A dominant session for either side can either shut the door on the opposition or open up a path to victory. For Bangladesh, this day is about breaking through the set partnership of the young Pakistani debutants and exposing the middle order to the turning ball. For Pakistan, the goal is to convert this solid start into a substantial first-innings lead. With a thunderstorm around, it will be keen to see how the weather plays and how can the Bangladesh bowlers benifit from the overcast conditions.

Pakistan’s second-day surge - The narrative shifted on Day 2 as Pakistan’s bowlers, led by a relentless Mohammad Abbas, clawed their way back into the contest. Abbas’s masterful five-wicket haul dismantled the Bangladeshi middle and lower order, eventually bowling the hosts out for 413. Not to be outdone, Pakistan’s batting unit responded with remarkable composure. Debutant Azan Awais played a standout innings, reaching a maiden Test half-century and remaining unbeaten on 85 by stumps. Along with Abdullah Fazal and a scratchy but crucial knock of 45 from Imam-ul-Haq, Pakistan reached 179/1, significantly narrowing the deficit and ensuring the second day belonged firmly to them.

Bangladesh’s opening statement - Hello and welcome to everyone tuning in. The first day of this encounter was a masterclass in resilience and aggression from the hosts. After Pakistan won the toss and elected to bowl on a greenish surface, Bangladesh found themselves under early pressure. However, captain Najmul Hossain Shanto rose to the occasion, hammering a magnificent, attacking century that stabilized the innings and shifted the momentum. Supported by solid half-centuries from Mominul Haque and the experienced Mushfiqur Rahim, Bangladesh ended the opening day in a commanding position, having turned a shaky start into a formidable foundation.

Day 2 concludes - The second day’s play concludes with Pakistan trailing in the contest, yet they find themselves in a promising position with almost their entire batting lineup still intact. While the match remains finely balanced, the upcoming sessions face a significant threat as rain and thunderstorms are forecast for Day 3. The action is scheduled to resume at 4 AM GMT on May 10, 2025, with both sides eager to see how the conditions influence the battle for control. Adios.

Pakistan are on top at the moment - Into the final stretch of the day, Pakistan kept their heads down and showed real grit. They pushed their score past the 100-run mark, looking entirely in control of the chase. But just when it seemed like a flawless finish for the visitors, Mehidy Hasan Miraz struck for Bangladesh, removing the dangerous Imam-ul-Haq for a well-made 45. At the halfway stage of the final session, Pakistan were 110/1. Even in the last phase of the day's play, Pakistani debutant just did not play the day out but they kept the foot on the accelerator and scored at a healthy clip. Azan remains unbeaten on 85 and is well set for the three-figure mark on his debut game, whereas Fazal was slow to kickstart but has picked up the pace of the game really well and will be heading into the dressing room with an unbeaten 37. Pakistan ends the day at 179 for 1 and are still trailing by 234 runs.

Pakistan started well in their innings - Going after a big total, Pakistan had absolutely no interest in just surviving. Openers Imam-ul-Haq and Azan Awais came out swinging with total confidence. They completely frustrated the Bangladesh pacers, smashing boundaries and racing to 50 for no loss by Tea. The pitch was nice to bat on and the Pakistan batters made the most of it.

Pakistan dominated post-Lunch as well - Pakistan ruthlessly cleaned up the tail, bowling Bangladesh out finally for 413. Abbas was absolutely surgical with his lines, finishing with a brilliant five-wicket haul. Shaheen Afridi delivered the knockout punch, knocking over Mushfiqur for a hard-fought 71 and ending a quick counter-attack from Taskin Ahmed. The momentum completely shifted into Pakistan's corner.

Abbas brought the heat on Day 2! Pakistan's bowlers finally woke up on Day 2. Mohammad Abbas was the absolute star, finding some life in the pitch and snapping up all three wickets to fall. Litton Das and Mehidy Hasan Miraz looked good early on but threw their wickets away. However, the veteran Mushfiqur Rahim stood like a wall, bringing up a gritty fifty to guide Bangladesh to a commanding 380/7 by the lunch break.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! The openers of Pakistan did very well to set the tone of the match. Bangladesh pacers tried their best to get early inroads but failed to get any. However, it's the experience of Mehidy Hasan Miraz that helped the side to get their first wicket and break the 106-run partnership. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of Day 2. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Imam-ul-Haq and Azan Awais will resume their innings. Nahid Rana to start with the ball. Lets go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Good start from Pakistan's openers - Pakistan then began their reply in the second session, with openers Imam-ul-Haq and debutant Azan Awais walking out to face a Bangladesh attack hungry for early inroads. Azan Awais has looked rock solid till this point, whereas Imam has been scratchy but is getting runs, which is the most important thing at this point for the visitors.  Pakistan went to Tea at 50 for no loss after 10 overs, with Azan Awais on 18, and Imam-ul-Haq on 28, still trailing Bangladesh by 363 runs. The openers have survived the initial burst, but with the surface deteriorating and Bangladesh's bowlers eager to exploit any footmarks, the evening session promises to be a stern examination of Pakistan's batting resolve, and one that could shape the entire course of this match-up. Alright folks, refill your snacks and join us back around 8.40 am GMT for the post-Tea break action.

A mountain to climb - Bangladesh were all out for 413 in their first innings, a total built on three standout knocks, Shanto's composed century, Mominul's elegant 91, and Mushfiqur Rahim's steady 71, which had put them in commanding control at the close of Day 1. The pitch has already begun to show clear signs of wear by this point, making the total an even more significant achievement for the hosts.

Pakistan fight back on Day 2 -  Bangladesh resumed the second session on Day 2 at 380 for 7 at Lunch, with Mushfiqur Rahim still at the crease, having produced another composed and patient innings to move into the seventies amid a crumbling lower order. Pakistan quickly resumed their disciplined effort with the ball, and Mohammad Abbas continued to probe relentlessly, targeting the right areas and picking up the remaining wickets, adding to an impressive five-wicket haul that had been the cornerstone of Pakistan's bowling effort throughout the innings. The Bangladesh tail offered some resistance, with Taskin Ahmed showing heart in playing some attacking strokes to help push the total further along, but ultimately Bangladesh were bowled out, with the final-wicket partnership at least ensuring the score was extended well beyond what Pakistan had hoped to restrict them to.
TEA ON DAY 1 - 18.1 overs were bowled in this session. 83 runs were scored and 3 wickets fell.
